subject: The output itself, traced bright along a chained survey baseline: each input pulse below the chain rings into a run of teeth one comb period apart, surveyed from a station whose bearing ray is the rotating light.
controls: pulse: the grey input pulse train under the chain line widens its pulses, and the bright teeth above widen with them (shape of the input path; the output tooth width follows as a second cue).
lens: the number and height of teeth each pulse rings into (shape of the bright output trace): one lone spike per pulse at 0, a long even run that fills the gap to the next pulse at 100.
sweep: the bearing ray from station a swings up from the chain line, with its angle arc (rotation, 8 to 48 degrees), and the tooth spacing breathes along the chainage as a second cue.
fog: grey survey contours roll in over the plan from the right edge, one more line every ~15 % (count), and the teeth tips flatten as the trace is low-passed.
reference: library/meikyu-capture/README.md (labelled wireframe ground, thin rails, mid-grey text that makes it read as authored)
risks: P3's own pitfall: at a glance it reads as an oscilloscope; the survey furniture (chain, chainage figures, station, offsets) is what makes it a plan and it has to stay.
Two controls (pulse, lens) both touch the bright trace; the rule holds only because pulse's primary is the grey input path. Perceptibility must prove it.
Fog by contour count is empty at the default 0, so the rest frame never shows fog; a contour lines' layer fighting the trace at 100 is untested.
Teeth 18 px apart at lens 100 approach hatching density; keep the comb period on screen ≥ 12 px whatever the note.
